name: Numerative Addition Coordination (with and)

dimensions.meaning: Additive composition of magnitude and addition
dimensions.distribution: Preferred in BrE; more formal registers

1.definition: Additive numerative formed by coordinating magnitude units and additions

constraints.description: Coordination targets numerative constituents; additions are coordinates (DP or NP).
Recursive: the addition coordinate can itself be a basic numerative or a magnitude phrase; its category may be DP or NP (category difference is tolerated under likeness of function).

projection.target: In three hundred and seven, each of three hundred and seven can denote a number independently. The whole normally denotes their sum and does not treat seven as another multiplier of hundred.
projection.evidence: Reynolds treats additions as coordinates and separates their distribution from that of factors.

curious.title: Big numbers said with and
curious.summary: Some numbers are built by joining a large amount and a small addition with the word and.
curious.body:
In two hundred and five, the word and joins two hundred and five. Together they make the sum. Two thousand and seven is built the same way: 2000 plus 7.

Each part can stand as a number on its own, and the whole means their sum. The seven in three hundred and seven isn't a second multiplier of hundred. This dictionary notes that this version is preferred in British English and in more formal speech.
curious.try: Say three hundred and seven aloud. Which parts could you say on their own as numbers?

teacher.summary: Shows that numbers like two hundred and five are additions, coordinating a magnitude and a smaller number.
teacher.explain: This construction forms an additive numerative by coordinating magnitude units and additions with and: two hundred and five means 200 + 5. The addition is a coordinate, and it can itself be a basic numerative or a magnitude phrase, so the pattern is recursive. In three hundred and seven, each of three hundred and seven can denote a number independently. The whole normally denotes their sum and doesn't treat seven as another multiplier of hundred. The dictionary notes that this form is preferred in British English and in more formal registers. It marks this account as provisional.
teacher.terms: Numerative is this grammar's term for number words, where a textbook may say numeral. Syndetic means joined with a coordinator.

contrasts.note: The same sum with no spoken and.

watch_for: A learner might read and in two hundred and five as joining two separate items rather than adding.
A learner might treat the seven in three hundred and seven as multiplying hundred.
teacher.activity: Students write number words for 105, 207 and 3004. They mark the large part and the addition, then compare with a partner.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Numerative Addition Coordination (with and)." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/numerative-addition-coordination-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, fa37529).
